name: Buy-side Counsel View (example)
description: Reflects arguments buy-side counsel commonly raises about three clauses this tool's built-in view calls neutral. It treats Close-out Amount (2002) as a real, if partial, win relative to the 1992 Loss standard it replaced — even though this tool's own baseline treats it as neutral in absolute terms. It also treats two 'neutral' fallback standards as functionally still dealer-favorable in practice: a recallable (rather than prohibited) rehypothecation right, given how often 'recall' proved slow or unenforceable in real dealer insolvencies (Lehman, MF Global); and an undefined 'reasonable time' fish-or-cut-bait standard, which in practice imposes little real constraint on a dealer's termination timing absent a fixed deadline.
